facts.statement: Kentrosaurus lived during the Late Jurassic period, specifically from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian ages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian to Tithonian),

facts.statement: The genus Kentrosaurus was described by the German paleontologist Edwin Hennig in 1915.
facts.quote: authority: Hennig, 1915

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Kentrosaurus is Kentrosaurus aethiopicus.
facts.quote: type_species: Kentrosaurus aethiopicus

facts.statement: Kentrurosaurus and Doryphorosaurus are considered junior objective synonyms of Kentrosaurus.
facts.quote: synonyms: Kentrurosaurus Hennig, 1916 Doryphorosaurus Nopcsa, 1916

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus is a genus of stegosaurid dinosaur found in the Lindi Region of Tanzania.
facts.quote: Kentrosaurus ( ; ) is a genus of stegosaurid dinosaur from the Late Jurassic in Lindi Region of Tanzania.

facts.statement: Recent cladistic analyses suggest Kentrosaurus is more derived than many other stegosaurs and is a close relative of Stegosaurus within the Stegosauridae.
facts.quote: Often thought to be a "primitive" member of the Stegosauria, several recent cladistic analyses find it as more derived than many other stegosaurs, and a close relative of Stegosaurus from the North American Morrison Formation within the Stegosauridae.

facts.statement: Fossils of Kentrosaurus aethiopicus are found exclusively in the Tendaguru Formation, dated to approximately 152 million years ago.
facts.quote: Fossils of K. aethiopicus have been found only in the Tendaguru Formation, dated to the late Kimmeridgian and early Tithonian ages, about 152 million years ago.

facts.statement: Hundreds of Kentrosaurus bones were unearthed by German expeditions in German East Africa between 1909 and 1912.
facts.quote: Hundreds of bones were unearthed by German expeditions to German East Africa between 1909 and 1912.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus coexisted with carnivorous theropods like Elaphrosaurus, giant sauropods like Giraffatitan, and the dryosaurid Dysalotosaurus in the Tendaguru Formation.
facts.quote: In the Tendaguru Formation, it coexisted with a variety of dinosaurs such as the carnivorous theropods Elaphrosaurus and Veterupristisaurus, giant herbivorous sauropods Giraffatitan and Tornieria, and the dryosaurid Dysalotosaurus.

facts.statement: Adult Kentrosaurus generally measured 4 to 4.5 meters in length and weighed between 700 and 1600 kilograms.
facts.quote: Kentrosaurus generally measured around 4 - 4.5 m in length as an adult, and weighed about 700 - 1600 kg.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus walked on all fours with straight hindlimbs.
facts.quote: It walked on all fours with straight hindlimbs.

facts.statement: The plates on Kentrosaurus gradually merged into spikes on the hips and tail.
facts.quote: These plates gradually merged into spikes on the hip and tail.

facts.statement: The longest spikes on Kentrosaurus were located on the tail and used for active defense.
facts.quote: The longest spikes were on the tail end and were used to actively defend the animal.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus possessed a long spike on each shoulder.
facts.quote: There also was a long spike on each shoulder.

facts.statement: Variations in thigh bone types suggest sexual dimorphism in Kentrosaurus, with one sex being larger and stouter.
facts.quote: The thigh bones come in two different types, suggesting that one sex was larger and more stout than the other.

facts.statement: The first Kentrosaurus fossils were discovered in 1909, identified as a stegosaur by Werner Janensch in 1910, and formally described by Edwin Hennig in 1915.
facts.quote: The first fossils of Kentrosaurus were discovered by the German Tendaguru Expedition in 1909, recognised as belonging to a stegosaur by expedition leader Werner Janensch on 24 July 1910, and described by German palaeontologist Edwin Hennig in 1915.

facts.statement: The name Kentrosaurus was coined by Hennig from Greek words meaning "sharp point" and "lizard".
facts.quote: The name Kentrosaurus was coined by Hennig and comes from the Greek /κέντρον, meaning "sharp point" or "prickle", and /σαῦρος meaning "lizard",

facts.statement: The specific name aethiopicus was added by Hennig to indicate the African origin of the fossils.
facts.quote: Hennig added the specific name aethiopicus to denote the provenance from Africa.

facts.statement: Hennig renamed the genus Kentrurosaurus in 1916, and Franz Nopcsa renamed a related genus Doryphorosaurus in the same year.
facts.quote: Hennig renamed his stegosaur Kentrurosaurus, "pointed-tail lizard", in 1916, while Hungarian paleontologist Franz Nopcsa renamed the genus Doryphorosaurus, "lance-bearing lizard", the same year.

facts.statement: Because the spelling differs from the ceratopsian Centrosaurus, Kentrosaurus remains the valid name while Kentrurosaurus and Doryphorosaurus are unnecessary replacement names.
facts.quote: However, because the spelling is different, both Doryphorosaurus and Kentrurosaurus are unneeded replacement names; Kentrosaurus remains the valid name for the genus with Kentrurosaurus and Doryphorosaurus being its junior objective synonyms.

facts.statement: Most remaining Kentrosaurus material is housed in the Museum für Naturkunde Berlin, with about 350 specimens, while the University of Tübingen holds a composite mount.
facts.quote: Today, almost all remaining material is housed in the Museum für Naturkunde Berlin (roughly 350 remaining specimens), while the museum of the Institute for Geosciences of the University of Tübingen houses a composite mount, roughly 50% of it being original bones.

facts.statement: Hennig designated a lectotype in 1925 consisting of the most complete partial skeleton, inventorised as MB.R.4800.1 through MB.R.4800.37.
facts.quote: In the original description, Hennig did not designate a holotype specimen. However, in a detailed monography on the osteology, systematic position and palaeobiology of Kentrosaurus in 1925, Hennig picked the most complete partial skeleton, today inventorised as MB.R.4800.1 through MB.R.4800.37, as a lectotype (see syntype).

facts.statement: The type locality for Kentrosaurus is Kindope, Tanzania, north of Tendaguru hill.
facts.quote: The type locality is Kindope, Tanzania, north of Tendaguru hill.

facts.statement: Heinrich Mallison clarified in 2011 that MB.R.4800 is the correct lectotype and that earlier material discovered before 1912 are paralectotypes.
facts.quote: In 2011, Heinrich Mallison clarified that all the material known to Hennig in 1915, i.e. all the bones discovered before 1912, when Hermann Heck concluded the last German excavations, are paralectotypes, and that MB.R.4800 is the correct lectotype.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus was a small stegosaur.
facts.quote: Kentrosaurus was a small stegosaur.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had a typical dinosaurian body plan with a small head, long neck, short forelimbs, long hindlimbs, and a long muscular tail.
facts.quote: It had the typical dinosaurian body bauplan, characterised by a small head, a long neck, short forelimbs and long hindlimbs, and a long, horizontal and muscular tail.

facts.statement: The long tail of Kentrosaurus placed its center of mass unusually far back for a quadrupedal animal.
facts.quote: The long tail of Kentrosaurus results in a position of the center of mass that is unusually far back for a quadrupedal animal.

facts.statement: The robust forelimbs of Kentrosaurus supported 10 to 15% of its bodyweight, assisting the hindlimbs in supporting the animal.
facts.quote: The hindlimbs, though powered by massive thigh muscles attached to a long ilium, did not support the animal alone, and the very robust forelimbs took up 10 to 15% of the bodyweight.

facts.statement: Powerful thigh muscles allowed Kentrosaurus to adopt a tripod stance using its hindlegs and tail.
facts.quote: The hindlimbs' thigh muscles were very powerful, allowing Kentrosaurus to reach a tripod stance on its hindlegs and tail.

facts.statement: Eight specimens consisting of skull, mandible, and teeth parts were collected from the Tendaguru Formation, mostly as isolated elements.
facts.quote: Eight specimens from the skull, mandible, and teeth have been collected and described from the Tendaguru Formation, most of them being isolated elements.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had a long and narrow skull that was small relative to its body size.
facts.quote: The long and narrow skull was small in proportion to the body.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the ridges on Kentrosaurus supported fleshy cheeks instead of a beak.
facts.quote: Other researchers have interpreted these ridges as modified versions of similar structures in other ornithischians which might have supported fleshy cheeks, rather than beaks.

facts.statement: The overall braincase morphology of Kentrosaurus is very similar to that of Tuojiangosaurus, Huayangosaurus, and Stegosaurus.
facts.quote: The overall braincase morphology is very similar to those of Tuojiangosaurus, Huayangosaurus, and Stegosaurus.

facts.statement: The Kentrosaurus brain was relatively short, deep, and small with strong cerebral and pontine flexures compared to other ornithischians.
facts.quote: The brain is relatively short, deep, and small, with a strong cerebral and pontine flexures and a steeply inclined posterodorsal edge when compared to those of other ornithischians.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus teeth were small, triangular, and flat, and wear facets indicate they were used to grind food.
facts.quote: Stegosaurian teeth were small, triangular, and flat; wear facets show that they did grind their food.

facts.statement: The Kentrosaurus neck consisted of 13 cervical vertebrae, with the first strongly fused to the skull and followed by the axis.
facts.quote: The neck was composed of 13 cervical (neck) vertebrae, the first being the atlas which was strongly fused to the occipital region of the skull and followed by the axis.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had 13 tall dorsal vertebrae with short centra.
facts.quote: The dorsal column consists of 13 dorsal (back) vertebrae which are tall and have short centra.

facts.statement: The Kentrosaurus sacrum consisted of 6 fused centra with transverse processes fused into a solid sacral plate.
facts.quote: The sacrum (part of pelvis with vertebrae) consists of 6 fused centra, the first being a loose sacrodorsal, while the rest of the centra's transverse processes (extensions of bone) are fused to the dorsal parts of the sacral ribs into a solid sacral plate.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had 29 caudal vertebrae, with 27 to 29 coossified for attaching to the tail spikes.
facts.quote: The caudal (tail) vertebrae are 29 in number, though 27-29 are coossified for attachment to the thagomizers (tail spikes).

facts.statement: The chevrons in the Kentrosaurus tail had the shape of an inverted T.
facts.quote: The chevrons, bones pointing to below from the bottom side of the tail vertebrae, have the shape of an inverted T.

facts.statement: The Kentrosaurus femur was the longest bone in its body, with the largest known specimen measuring 665 mm.
facts.quote: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest element in the body, with the largest known femur measuring 665 mm from the proximal to distal end.

facts.statement: The Kentrosaurus foot ended in 3 toes, each bearing a hoof-like claw.
facts.quote: The pes (foot) terminated in 3 toes, all of which had hoof-like unguals (claws).

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus possessed extensive bony armor covering its body, including small plates likely on the neck and front trunk, and spikes of various shapes.
facts.quote: Typically for a stegosaur, Kentrosaurus had extensive osteoderm (bony structures in the skin) covering, including small plates (probably located on the neck and anterior trunk), and spikes of various shapes.

facts.statement: One specimen of Kentrosaurus had a spike with a bone core measuring 731 millimetres in length.
facts.quote: The spikes of Kentrosaurus are very elongated, with one specimen having a bone core length of 731 millimetres.

facts.statement: Researchers believe the spikes and plates of Kentrosaurus were likely covered by a layer of horn.
facts.quote: The spikes and plates were likely covered by horn.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence shows a pair of closely spaced spikes attached to the tail tip and other spikes regularly spaced in pairs along the tail.
facts.quote: A pair of closely spaced spikes was found articulated with a tail tip, and a number of spikes were found apparently regularly spaced in pairs along the path of an articulated tail.

facts.statement: Hennig and Janensch identified four types of armor elements that changed shape from short plates at the front to long spikes at the rear, suggesting a continuous distribution of fifteen pairs along the body.
facts.quote: Hennig and Janensch, while grouping the dermal armour elements into four distinct types, recognised an apparently continuous change of shape among them, shorter and flatter plates at the front gradually merging into longer and more pointed spikes towards the rear, suggesting an uninterrupted distribution along the entire body, in fifteen pairs.

facts.statement: One specific type of Kentrosaurus spike is strongly asymmetrical with a very broad base, differing from all other spike types.
facts.quote: There is one type of spike that differs from all others in being strongly, and not only slightly, asymmetrical, and having a very broad base.

facts.statement: There is a debate over the location of a specific asymmetrical spike: classic reconstructions placed it on the hips, while recent reconstructions suggest it was on the shoulder based on comparisons with Chinese stegosaurs.
facts.quote: Because of bone morphology classic reconstructions placed it on the hips, at the iliac blade, while many recent reconstructions place it on the shoulder, because a similarly shaped spike is known to have existed on the shoulder in the Chinese stegosaurs Gigantspinosaurus and Huayangosaurus.

facts.statement: Hennig assigned Kentrosaurus to the family Stegosauridae in 1915 based on dermal armor and angled neural spines on the tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: In Hennig's 1915 description, Kentrosaurus was assigned to the family Stegosauridae due to the preservation of dermal armor and features like posterodorsally angled neural spines on the caudal vertebrae.

facts.statement: The only accepted species of Kentrosaurus is Kentrosaurus aethiopicus, which was named by Hennig in 1915.
facts.quote: The type and sole accepted species of Kentrosaurus is Kentrosaurus aethiopicus, named by Hennig in 1915.

facts.statement: Fossils originally named Stegosaurus longispinus were classified as Kentrosaurus longispinus in 1993, but this was rejected by the community, leading to the creation of the separate genus Alcovasaurus due to differences in tail spikes and pelvic structure.
facts.quote: Fragmentary fossil material from Wyoming, named Stegosaurus longispinus by Charles Gilmore in 1914, was in 1993 classified as a North American species of Kentrosaurus, as K. longispinus. However, this action was not accepted by the paleontological community, and S. longispinus has been assigned to its own genus, Alcovasaurus, differing from Kentrosaurus in having more elongated tail spikes and the structure of the pelvis and vertebrae.

facts.statement: A 2025 phylogenetic analysis suggests Kentrosaurus belongs to the subfamily Dacentrurinae, though this contradicts its traditional placement in Stegosauridae.
facts.quote: In 2025, phylogenetic analysis conducted by Sánchez-Fenollosa & Cobos recovered Kentrosaurus as a member of Dacentrurinae.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus was a herbivore that swallowed large chunks of food with little chewing.
facts.quote: Like all ornithischians, Kentrosaurus was a herbivore. The fodder was barely chewed and swallowed in large chunks.

facts.statement: It is hypothesized that Kentrosaurus was a low-level browser that ate foliage and fruit from non-flowering plants.
facts.quote: One hypothesis on stegosaurid diet holds that they were low-level browsers, eating foliage and low-growing fruit from various non-flowering plants.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus could reach vegetation up to 1.7 meters high while standing on all fours.
facts.quote: Kentrosaurus was capable of eating at heights of up to 1.7 m when on all fours.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus may have been able to rear up on its hind legs to reach higher vegetation in trees.
facts.quote: It may also have been possible for it to rear up on its hindlegs to reach vegetation higher in trees.

facts.statement: If Kentrosaurus reared up on its hind legs, it could potentially feed at heights of 3.3 meters.
facts.quote: In this pose, Kentrosaurus could have fed at heights of 3.3 m.

facts.statement: The tail of Kentrosaurus was likely too flexible to function as a 'third leg' for support, contrary to suggestions by Robert Thomas Bakker.
facts.quote: it was not stiff enough to function as a "third leg" as had been suggested by Robert Thomas Bakker.

facts.statement: Holly Barden and Susannah Maidment concluded that Kentrosaurus exhibited sexual dimorphism based on differences in femur proportions rather than size.
facts.quote: Differences in the proportions, not the size, of the femurs (thighbones) led Holly Barden and Susannah Maidment to realize that Kentrosaurus probably showed sexual dimorphism.

facts.statement: The ratio of robust to gracile femurs was 2:1, suggesting that the more common robust form likely represented females.
facts.quote: The occurrence ratio of the robust morph to the gracile one was 2:1, and it is likely that the higher percentage of animals were females.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the femur ratio accurately reflects sexual dimorphism because the studied specimens likely did not represent a single contemporary population.
facts.quote: The problem posed by the ratio is that the multiple specimens studied, died in the same place, but probably not in a sudden mass-death and so do not represent a single herd or contemporary population.

facts.statement: Due to armor obstacles, it is possible that Kentrosaurus pairs mated back-to-back with the female in a lordosis posture.
facts.quote: As the plates and spikes would have been obstacles during copulation, it is possible that pairs mated back-to-back with the female staying still in a lordosis posture as the male maneuvers his penis into her cloaca.

facts.statement: A 2013 study found that Kentrosaurus had a higher growth rate than Stegosaurus and Scutellosaurus, indicated by rapid deposition of vascularized bone.
facts.quote: In 2013, a study by Ragna Redelstorff e.a. concluded that the bone histology of Kentrosaurus indicated that it had a higher growth rate than reported for Stegosaurus and Scutellosaurus, in view of the relatively rapid deposition of highly vascularised fibrolamellar bone.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had a highly mobile tail containing at least forty vertebrae.
facts.quote: Because the tail had at least forty caudal vertebrae, it was highly mobile.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the tail could swing in an arc of 180 degrees.
facts.quote: It could possibly swing at an arc of 180 degrees, covering the entire half circle behind it.

facts.statement: The tail tip may have swung at speeds as high as 50 km/h.
facts.quote: Swing speeds at the tail end may have been as high as 50 km/h.

facts.statement: Earlier interpretations suggested Kentrosaurus might have charged rearward to run through attackers like modern porcupines.
facts.quote: Earlier interpretations of the defensive behaviour of Kentrosaurus included the suggestion that the animal might have charged to the rear, to run through attackers with its spines, in the way of modern porcupines.

facts.statement: It is hypothesized that Kentrosaurus adopted a sprawling posture when defending itself.
facts.quote: It is hypothesised that the animal adopted a sprawling posture when defending itself.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus lived in what is now Tanzania during the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: Kentrosaurus lived in what is now Tanzania in the Late Jurassic Tendaguru Formation.

facts.statement: The main quarries for Kentrosaurus are located in the Middle Saurian Beds dating from the upper Kimmeridgian.
facts.quote: The main Kentrosaurus quarries were located in the Middle Saurian Beds dating from the upper Kimmeridgian.

facts.statement: Since 2012, the boundary between the Kimmeridgian and Tithonian has been dated to 152.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Since 2012, the boundary between the Kimmeridgian and Tithonian is dated at 152.1 million year ago.

facts.statement: The genus Kentrosaurus was described by Edwin Hennig in 1915.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Edwin Hennig, 1915

facts.statement: The species K. aethiopicus was described by Hennig in 1915.
facts.quote: species_authority: Hennig, 1915

facts.statement: Synonyms for Kentrosaurus aethiopicus include Doryphorosaurus aethiopicus, Kentrorosaurus aethiopicus, Kentrosaurus aethiopus, and Kentrurosaurus aethiopicus.
facts.quote: synonyms: Doryphorosaurus aethiopicus Nopcsa, 1916 Kentrorosaurus aethiopicus Young, 1944 Kentrosaurus aethiopus Chinsamy, 1997 Kentrurosaurus aethiopicus Hennig, 1916

facts.statement: Hundreds of bones were unearthed by German expeditions in East Africa between 1909 and 1912.
facts.quote: Cientos de huesos fueron desenterrados por las expediciones alemanas al África oriental alemana entre 1909 y 1912.

facts.statement: Adult Kentrosaurus generally measured around 4.5 meters in length and weighed approximately 1.1 tons.
facts.quote: Kentrosaurus generalmente medía alrededor de 4,5 metros de longitud como adulto, y pesaba aproximadamente una 1,1 toneladas.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had a row, possibly double, of small plates running down its neck and back.
facts.quote: Tenía una fila, probablemente doble, de platos pequeños que le bajaban por el cuello y la espalda.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had a long spine on each shoulder.
facts.quote: También había una espina larga en cada hombro.

facts.statement: The femur bones come in two different types, suggesting sexual dimorphism in size and robustness.
facts.quote: Los huesos del muslo vienen en dos tipos diferentes, lo que sugiere que un sexo era más grande y más robusto que el otro.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus was a small stegosaurid.
facts.quote: Kentrosaurus era un pequeño estegosáurido.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had a typical stegosaur body plan characterized by a small head, long neck, short forelimbs, long hindlimbs, and a long, horizontal, muscular tail.
facts.quote: Tenía el típico plan corporal de estos dinosaurios, caracterizado por una cabeza pequeña, un cuello largo, extremidades anteriores cortas y extremidades posteriores largas, y una cola larga, horizontal y musculosa.

facts.statement: Only a single complete tooth was known when Hennig published his monograph in 1925.
facts.quote: Solo se conocía un solo diente completo cuando Hennig publicó su monografía en 1925.

facts.statement: A reconstructed skeleton of Kentrosaurus at the Museum für Naturkunde in Berlin measures 4.5 meters from snout to tail tip.
facts.quote: La longitud total de una montura esquelética compuesta en el Museum für Naturkunde de Berlín, Alemania, desde la punta del hocico hasta la punta de la cola es de 4,5 metros.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated that a 4-meter-long Kentrosaurus weighed 700 kilograms.
facts.quote: En 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimó el peso de un Kentrosaurus de 4 metros de largo, en 700 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Mallison estimated the mass of the 4.5-meter-long Berlin skeleton between 1 and 1 tons, depending on the reconstructed tail musculature.
facts.quote: Una estimación para el montaje compuesto de 4,5 metros de largo en el Museum für Naturkunde Berlin de Mallison, sobre la base de un esqueleto virtual 3D y un modelo 3D, varió entre 1073 L y 1267 L, y una masa corporal entre 1 y 1, toneladas, dependiendo de la cantidad de musculatura reconstruida para la cola.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had an unusually rearward center of mass for a quadruped due to its long tail.
facts.quote: La larga cola del Kentrosaurus da como resultado una posición del centro de masa que está inusualmente muy atrás para un animal cuadrúpedo.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had straight femurs indicating a vertical limb posture, unlike typical bipeds.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, los fémures son rectos en Kentrosaurus, a diferencia de los bípedos típicos, lo que indica una posición de extremidad recta y vertical.

facts.statement: The robust forelimbs of Kentrosaurus supported 10% to 15% of its body weight.
facts.quote: las extremidades anteriores muy robustas ocupaban del 10 al 15% del peso corporal.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus neural spines on the tail did not run subparallel like in most dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Lo más notable es que las espinas neurales, las extensiones superiores de las vértebras en forma de cuchilla, en la cola no corren subparalelas, como en la mayoría de los dinosaurios.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus tail spines pointed backward in the front third, were nearly vertical in the middle third, and hooked forward obliquely at the rear.
facts.quote: En el tercio delantero de la cola, apuntan hacia atrás, en la dirección habitual. Sin embargo, en la cola media, son casi verticales, y más atrás tienen forma de gancho y apuntan oblicuamente hacia adelante.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus dorsal vertebrae had neural arches more than twice as high as the centrum, with a very spacious neural canal.
facts.quote: También es típico que las vértebras dorsales tengan un arco neural más del doble de alto que el centro, el cuerpo vertebral, y casi completamente ocupado por el canal neural extremadamente espacioso.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had rod-shaped transverse processes on the front tail vertebrae with narrow bases that did not touch the fused sacral plate.
facts.quote: Los procesos transversales de las vértebras de la cola frontal tienen forma de varilla con bases estrechas y no tocan la placa formada por la fusión de los procesos de las vértebras sacras.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had inverted T-shaped chevrons pointing downward from the underside of the tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: Los galones, huesos que apuntan hacia abajo desde el lado inferior de las vértebras de la cola, tienen la forma de una T invertida.

facts.statement: In Kentrosaurus, the ilium was equal to or longer than the femur.
facts.quote: La longitud del ilion es igual o mayor que la del fémur.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had extensive dermal armor including small plates likely on the neck and anterior trunk, and variously shaped spines.
facts.quote: Como es típico para un estegosáurido, Kentrosaurus tenía una amplia cobertura de osteodermos, estructuras óseas en la piel, que incluía pequeñas placas, probablemente ubicadas en el cuello y el tronco anterior y espinas de varias formas.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus spines were very long, with one specimen having a bone core length of 731 millimeters.
facts.quote: Las espinas de Kentrosaurus son muy alargadas, con un espécimen que tiene una longitud del núcleo óseo de 731 milímetros.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus plates had a thickened middle section, resembling modified spines.
facts.quote: Las placas tienen una sección engrosada en el medio, como si fueran espinas modificadas.

facts.statement: Hennig and Janensch identified 15 pairs of dermal armor elements that gradually changed from short flat plates in the front to long sharp spines in the back.
facts.quote: Hennig y Janensch, al agrupar los elementos de la armadura dérmica en cuatro tipos distintos, reconocieron un cambio aparentemente continuo de forma entre ellos, placas más cortas y más planas en la parte delantera fusionándose gradualmente en espinas más largas y puntiagudas hacia la parte posterior, sugiriendo una distribución ininterrumpida a lo largo de todo el cuerpo, en 15 pares.

facts.statement: While classic reconstructions placed a unique robust Kentrosaurus spine on the hips, recent reconstructions place it on the shoulder based on similarities in Chinese stegosaurs.
facts.quote: Debido a la morfología ósea, las reconstrucciones clásicas la colocaron en las caderas, en la lámina ilíaca, mientras que muchas reconstrucciones recientes la colocan en el hombro, porque se sabe que existió una espina de forma similar en el hombro en los estegosáuridos chinos Gigantspinosaurus y Huayangosaurus.

facts.statement: The genus Kentrosaurus was named by Hennig in 1915.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Kentrosaurus (genus), Hennig 1915

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus belongs to the subfamily Dacentrurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Dacentrurinae

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus is classified in the family Stegosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Stegosauridae

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus is a member of the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus lived from the Oxfordian to the Tithonian stages, between 161.5 and 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Oxfordian to Tithonian (161.5 to 143.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: A partial lectotype specimen of Kentrosaurus was excavated from the 'St' site in Kindope, Tendaguru, Tanzania.
facts.quote: miniaturadeimagen|derecha|Lectotipo, individuo parcial de la excavación 'St' en Kindope, Tendaguru, Tanzania.

facts.statement: A pair of closely spaced tail spines articulated with the tail tip, and several other spines were found regularly spaced in pairs along the articulated tail.
facts.quote: Se encontró un par de espinas estrechamente espaciadas articuladas con una punta de cola, y se encontraron varias espinas aparentemente separadas regularmente en pares a lo largo del camino de una cola articulada.

rejected.quote: It had a small, elongated head with a beak used to bite off plant material that would be digested in a large gut.
